frontier.hypothesis: The v12 rematerialization residual (extra li s3,0x12 at position 30 vs target's single li at position 114) is likely a first-pass scheduler hoisting decision independent of C source placement -- 4 distinct spellings (s3: no-initializer, reordered decl, moved statement; s6: split into two locals) all failed to move it, and 2 more spellings (s6: type-narrow, decl-order-swap) also failed. The remaining untried axis is changing what ELSE occupies the early scheduling slot so the li has scheduling competition, rather than changing v12 itself.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c first-pass list scheduler (schedule_block) picks the earliest available slot for a no-dependency constant load; if no other ready insn competes for that slot, the li floats to the top regardless of source position.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_80073200/dumps/text1b.sched around insn 11's scheduling decision to see what OTHER insns were candidates for that early slot, and whether introducing a genuine dependency chain (not v12 itself, but an adjacent statement) before v12's first use changes the competition.

frontier.hypothesis: The s1/v1 register-seat tie (hunks 10/11/16/17: target addiu s1,v0,12 / sw s1,28(sp) vs ours v1) is unaffected by declaration-order changes to either tbl or s1 in isolation (tbl tested this session, s1 itself not yet retried) -- likely coupled to the same allocation pass that resolves the v12 residual, per the s5 note.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno priority / register class preference for the s1 pseudo, potentially entangled with the same long-range materialization decisions governing v12.
frontier.next_probe: Once frontier item 1 (v12 rematerialization) has a genuine lever, re-diff before spending a dedicated session on the s1/v1 tie in isolation -- per the s5 coupling note, it may shift as a side effect.

frontier.hypothesis: The D_800A3580 lh-vs-lw width residual (hunk12: target lh v1,0(gp) / ours lw v1,0(gp)) is a narrower sub-word-read lever candidate ([[narrow-stack-param-subword-offset]] family) untried on this global read.
frontier.mechanism: GCC widens the D_800A3580 read to lw because of surrounding value liveness (per candidate.c's session-4 header note); a narrow-width C-level cast might force the lh form.
